newsitem.title: FRANCE: Criminal Sobhraj lands in France from India.
newsitem.headline: Criminal Sobhraj lands in France from India.

text.p: Notorious criminal Charles Sobhraj, released after 20 years in Indian prisons, arrived in Paris on Tuesday and was whisked away to police headquarters for checks on his criminal record and claim for French citizenship.

Police sources said he was escorted to criminal police headquarters in Nanterre, west of Paris, after landing at 6.40 a.m. (0440 GMT) aboard Air France flight 147 at Paris's Charles de Gaulle from Delhi.
They said Sobhraj was being questioned as a witness in a probe of accusations by an unnamed French woman who claimed to have suffered a poisoning attempt in India.
Justice Ministry sources said police were also checking whether he was entitled to French citizenship and residence.
Reporters waited in vain for a glimpse of the man who served two decades in prison in India on a string of charges including murder and robbery committed against tourists across Asia.
Sobhraj's lawyer Jacques Verges, saying his client was legally a free man, angrily left the airport without seeing him and threatened to take legal action if he was not released soon.
"I shall make enquiries with French authorities and, if he should be held longer, I shall lodge a complaint," he said.
Whatever Sobhraj may have done was covered by France's statute of limitations which bans prosecution after 10 years, he told reporters.
"If the law is applied, there is no legal basis to prosecute him in France, whether some people like it or not," he said.
"This melodrama...for a Frenchman who is coming home after having served his sentence and against whom no proceedings exist, shows the state's weakness, not strength," he said.
Sobhraj was first arrested in India for holding up a hotel jewellery shop in 1971. He was later charged with a long string of crimes, serving time for some and being acquitted in others.

India ordered him deported in February but France refused to accept him pending checks on his past record and nationality claim. Paris eventually agreed on Monday that Sobhraj, who was born to an Indian father and Vietnamese mother, had a strong claim for French citizenship.
French Foreign Ministry spokesman Yves Doutriaux said he would have to apply for a certificate of citizenship from a judge, but indicated it would be a formality.
Two officials of India's Foreigners' Regional Registration Office (FRRO) accompanied Sobhraj to Paris.

Sobhraj, whose criminal exploits have been the subject of two books, plans to concentrate on working on a $15 million English-language film based on his life, to be produced in France with American actors. He has said he would write the script but would not play the title role.
He was philosophical as he left Delhi. "I have no choice," he told reporters, adding he would definitely return to India where he has two half-sisters.
He had said in the past that he longed to roam the streets of Paris to enjoy his freedom. "I want to take a walk on the bank of the River Seine in Paris," he said.
